_about: Hand-maintained rules and assumptions. tools/build_data.py never overwrites this file. Every entry carries a 'basis': 'documented' = stated by the game or a guide, 'observed' = taken from real unit data, 'assumed' = our best guess, change it if you learn better.

attackSpeed.note: AS = Spd - max(0, weapon Wt - Bld). Avoid uses the same value. (Game8 Attack Speed Guide)

hit.note: Hit = weapon Hit + Dex. The game only says Hit is 'affected by Dex'; the coefficient follows Three Houses.

crit.note: Crit = weapon Crit + Dex/2. The game only says Crit is 'affected by Dex'.

dodge.note: Dodge = Lck. The game only says Dodge is 'affected by Lck'.

playerBldPerLevel.note: Bld is not a level-up stat but rises over the game: Lv1 units have Bld 1-2, Lv39-40 units 3-5, a Lv63 unit 7. Modeled as +0.07 per level from the unit's join value.

gauntletAvoid.note: Gauntlets have 'inherently high Avoid'; the size of the bonus is not published.

displayedHitIsTrueHit.note: Rolls use the displayed percentage (single RN). Unknown whether the game averages two RNs.

progression.note: Recommended unit levels for each license tier (Game8 class change guide). Master licenses unlock in Part III.
progression.divineNote: Divine licenses are one-per-playthrough key items found late in Part III; the level is assumed and divine classes are only searched with --divine.

checkpoints.note: One checkpoint per story chapter. playerLevel is the level a regularly used unit is expected to have; enemyLevel is the generic enemy level and bosses sit at bossLevel. Anchors from real data: Part I Ch.1 enemies Lv1 / boss Lv4, Ch.2 boss Lv6, Ch.3 boss Lv7, Ch.4 boss Lv11, a Lv30 unit joining in Ch.9, a Lv39 unit joining in Part II Ch.3, Lv40 generics and a Lv45 boss in the prologue preview, a Lv63 unit joining after Part III section 5. Everything between the anchors is interpolated.

tierByLevel.note: Generic enemies seen so far use Beginner classes below Lv20 (Gladiator Lv1/Lv10), Specialty at Lv20, Advanced at Lv35-40 and a Master-class boss at Lv45.

bossWeight.note: Weight of each modeled boss relative to a modeled generic (1.0). Real (observed) enemies get observedWeight.

observedWeight.note: A real enemy counts this many times as much as its modeled counterpart (a real boss weighs observedWeight * bossWeight).

observedLevelWindow.note: A real enemy joins a checkpoint's roster when its level is within this many levels of the checkpoint's enemy or boss level.

hardDelta.note: Hard minus Normal for the one boss published on both difficulties (Lind, Lv45 High Savant). Applied flat to every enemy with --hard.

defaultBld.note: Lv1 generics show Bld 2; Lv40 generics Bld 2-3.

weaponPriority.note: A modeled enemy wields its class's main weapon type: the largest Skill EXP bonus on the class page, ties broken in this order.

arsenal.note: Standard gear a unit is assumed to own at a given level, and what generic enemies carry. Player unlock levels follow the weapon-rank requirements of each license tier (D by Lv5, C by Lv20, B by Lv35, A by Lv45); enemy levels follow observed inventories (wooden Lv1, bronze Lv4-10, iron Lv20-35, silver Lv40). Relics, forged +N weapons and low-use spells are left out; of the special weapons only those under 'magical' are carried.

thrown.note: Thrown weapons (range 1-2) every unit is assumed to carry alongside its melee weapons once it has the level and the skill rank. Player unlock levels are assumed to follow the standard tiers. Without these no melee class could attack from range 2, and abilities such as Esmeralda's Throwing Arm could never apply.

magical.note: Weapons of a physical type that are 'treated as a magical attack': they strike with Mag against Res and count towards magDmg, so a sword class has a magic option. Carried like the thrown weapons, once the unit has the level and the skill rank (Levin Sword is rank C, so the Da Mina tier's level). Like every weapon here its durability is not modelled, so unlike a spell it does not run out during a map. --no-magic-weapons leaves them out. The magical gauntlets are left out: Zerberus is Troy's own, Salamander and Zerberus have 3 and 5 uses, and Breidablik is a Might 2 bonus item.

scrolls.note: Dark spells any unit can be taught from a scroll, on top of its own spell list: no skill rank is asked for, only a class that casts black magic. 'player' is the level of the chapter the scroll can first be had: Mire and Death are traded for at the Vandahl Trading Company from about Part I Ch.10, the Dark Spikes scroll is in a Part III chest. A scroll teaches one unit, so this is what one unit could have, not what a whole army can. Left out: Swarm and Banshee (when their scrolls can be had is not recorded), Luna (no scroll found) and the single-use Fimbulvetr Night and Agnea's Arrow. Death's 'high Crit' has no published number and is not counted. --no-scrolls leaves them all out. (Community spreadsheet, Reason tab.)

fallbackHeals.note: Player units use their own published spell list (data/characters.json) at the ranks it gives. A unit whose list is not published yet falls back to the 'spells' above, gated by level and skill rank, and to these heals.

scoring.note: Legacy duel score (--role duel only). How one checkpoint's results become a 0-100 score. Offense = dealPP * (share of enemy HP removed when the unit attacks) + koPP * (chance to kill in that one attack) + dealEP * (share removed when countering an enemy's attack). Bulk looks at the share of the unit's own HP lost per combat (takenEP of it from being attacked, the rest from counters taken when attacking): losing bulkCeil or less scores 100, losing bulkFloor or more scores 0, linear between. Score = 100 * (offense*Offense + bulk*Bulk). Override the offense/bulk split with --offense.

skills.note: Skill ranks are not simulated by the game data we have, so they are estimated from exposure: every level spent in a class that trains a skill (a weapon it wields, or Riding / Flying / Heavy Armor / Infantry for its type; a Commoner trains every weapon) adds 1 - the unit is assumed to keep every weapon type its class wields in practice - times 'preferred' for a skill the unit is proficient in and 'nonIdeal' for one it is bad at. A rank is reached at the exposure listed. Thresholds are set so a unit that trains one skill from its Beginner class meets the C / B / A exams at the recommended Lv20 / 35 / 45. Ranks gate weapons (Iron D, Da Mina C, Silver B), each unit's own spells, and class exams.

maxExamGap.note: A class is offered only if every exam requirement is within this many ranks of the unit's estimated rank; the shortfall is what Arena training and manuals would have to cover and is reported as the path's training need. --free-reclass lifts the limit.

lateJoinerSkills.note: A unit that joins already promoted is given the ranks its join class's exam asks for, plus exposure in the skills that class trains as if it had held the class since the previous tier.

lateJoiners.note: Units whose published stat line is not their join state. 'from' is the first checkpoint they can be fielded at (Game8 recruit pages); 'class' is the class Game8's class guide starts them from (assumed where the join class itself is not published). Their level is that checkpoint's enemy level and their stats are grown from the Lv1 estimate (or the published guest line) with their own growth rates - an estimate, flagged '*'.

abilities.note: Personal abilities and abilities learned by level are read from their in-game text (src/abilities.js). Every learned ability is assumed to be active at once (the game may limit equipped abilities). A 'Trigger %' effect is applied at its average value. Conditions on HP assume the unit is at full HP. Effects that depend on position, allies, Blaze arts, status effects or earlier combats in the map are not scored; `char` lists them.

combatArts.note: A bonus 'when attacking with a (bow) combat art' is counted in every fight the unit starts with a fitting weapon, as if it always attacked with a combat art. The art's own might, hit and cost are not modelled, so this is the ability's bonus alone, and the unit only earns it by using its arts; `char`, `all` and the site state that caveat. Affects Inyoni (Pierce) and Tobias (Power Arts, All-Out Attack).

adjacentAllies.note: Allies assumed adjacent for 'for each adjacent ally' effects.

profile.note: A unit is described by separate 0-100 axes, each measured at every checkpoint against that checkpoint's reference enemies. physDmg / magDmg: how well its best physical / magical option kills in attacks the unit starts, averaged over the reference enemies: 'oneAttackKill' of it is the chance to kill outright in one attack, the rest kill speed - 100 / the number of attacks it expects to need (hit, crit and follow-up chances played out) - so damage counts by the kills it buys and not by the HP it removes. safety: share of the unit's own HP it keeps during that attack (100 = the enemy cannot answer, as against a bow or spell from range 2). The three defensive measures that follow are taken with the weapon the unit is left holding (see 'heldWeapon'). physBulk / magBulk: share of the unit's own HP left after one attack a physical / magical reference enemy starts, if every strike lands. avoid: chance a reference enemy's strike misses. physSurv / magSurv: the small fights a unit is actually left in - attacked by one physical / magical reference enemy, by two, up to 'enemyPhaseAttacks', played out with hit and crit chances - and the share of its HP it has left on average after each (dead = none). Bulk and avoid combined, so an armored unit and a dodging unit are compared on what they walk away with. Every axis is measured at 'statLines' whole-number stat lines and averaged. support: HP healed per map as a share of 'healBars' ally HP bars (plus 'dance' for a class that can Dance). reach: movement, from 'movFloor' (0) to 'movCeil' (100), fliers count 'flyingMov' extra. bestDmg is the larger of physDmg and magDmg.

references.note: The generic enemies every axis is measured against: made-up but plausible, because too few real ones are published to fill a chapter. One list per enemy tier (the checkpoint's enemy level picks the tier, see enemies.tierByLevel). Each row is one enemy: a class, the weapon it carries (a weapon type takes the best standard enemy weapon of that type for its level; a weapon name is that exact weapon) and its level relative to the checkpoint's enemy level (default 0). Stats come from the fitted enemy model. Levels are spread two either side of the chapter's level, upwards only in the Beginner tier because Lv1 is the floor; thrown axes and spears are included because the published bosses Goliath and Zarcone carry Hand Axes. 'archetype' is only a label for grouping, except that the first 'fighter' is the typical ally whose HP the support axis heals. Every row counts equally, so the mix is the weighting: about a sixth each of armour, fighters and riders, an eighth each of swordsmen, archers and fliers (no flier in the Beginner tier), and a sixth magic. An enemy that attacks with magic is used for magBulk and magSurv, the rest for physBulk and physSurv; all of them for damage and avoid. Rows that come out identical at a checkpoint are counted once.

combatsPerMap.note: Attacks a unit makes per map. Spells have limited uses (doubled or tripled by Seeker / Zenith class abilities); magDmg averages the best spells that fit into this many attacks, and an attack with no spell left counts as zero. --no-cast-limit lifts the limit on attack spells (not on heals), as if the unit rested between fights: every attack is then its best spell.

heldWeapon.note: A unit cannot change weapon between its own attack and the enemy's answer, so it defends with the weapon it attacked with. Each weapon is held for the share of the reference enemies the unit attacks with it (its faster kill of physical and magical; spells by the casts they fill), and bulk, avoid and survival are averaged with those shares. A class with gauntlets therefore gets their Avoid only when it also attacks with them. A unit that cannot hurt any reference enemy counts every weapon equally. The game does let a unit that does not attack end its turn holding anything; that is not modelled.

oneAttackKill.note: Share of a damage axis given to killing outright in the one attack the unit starts (its follow-up included); the rest goes to kill speed. A kill that takes two attacks leaves an enemy alive to answer, so a unit that kills in one counts for more than twice one that needs two. 0 = kill speed alone.

enemyPhaseAttacks.note: The most attackers a unit is measured against at once. physSurv / magSurv average the HP it has left after 1, 2, ... this many attacks in a row, each from a physical / magical reference enemy picked at random. 3 = one-on-one, one-on-two and one-on-three: a unit is assumed to be healed or pulled back before a longer beating, which is why this is not a whole enemy phase.

statLines.note: Level-up luck is not averaged away: a unit is measured at this many whole-number stat lines per chapter, spread from unlucky to lucky in every stat, and the axes are the average over them. Kill and survival thresholds therefore count for the share of playthroughs that actually reach them.

healCastsPerMap.note: Most heals one unit can cast in a map (one per turn).

healFormula.note: HP restored = spell power + Mag / 3 (+ class and personal heal bonuses). The game only says healing scales with Mag; the divisor follows Three Houses.

healAreaTargets.note: Allies an area heal (Fortify) is assumed to reach.

healBars.note: Healing this many full HP bars of a typical ally (the fighter reference's HP) per map scores support 100.

dance.note: Support score given for being able to Dance (an extra action for an ally each turn). No published numbers; a judgment call.

search.note: How class paths are searched. A unit may change class between any two chapters, to a class of its current tier or higher whose license level it has reached and whose exam is within maxExamGap: so promotions can be taken late and a tier can hold more than one class. The search keeps, for every class the unit could hold at a chapter, the 'beam' best histories per role and drops the rest.

detours.note: Sideways class changes (to another class of the same tier) allowed along one path (--detours). Moving up a tier is always allowed.

minLevels.note: Levels a unit spends in a class before it changes again: a class is not put on for a single chapter. The class a unit joins in is exempt.

beam.note: Histories kept per class and role at every chapter. Higher = more alternatives listed and a more thorough search, slower.

margin.note: A history is only kept as one of its class's best if, in at least one role, it is within this many points (campaign average) of the leading history. Each class's single best history per role is always kept.

tidy.note: After the search, each role's best this-many paths are retried with each class change dropped and with each taken as early as the rules allow; legal variants join the list.

screen.note: Candidates for a class change are first measured at their expected stats only; this many times 'beam' of them per class and role go on to the full measurement.

parents.note: For each class and role, how many of the best-scoring states are tried as the state that changes into it.

parentMargin.note: A state is only tried as a parent if its score so far is within this many points, per chapter still to play, of the best eligible parent: the most a better stat spread could plausibly make up.

roles.note: A role is a weighting of the profile axes; paths are ranked per role, never across roles. Weights are a judgment call - edit them or add roles. The three tank roles weigh survival alone (two parts the named kind to one of the other, equal for the mixed tank): with damage in, a 'magic tank' was picked for its Str. No role weights reach: as a flat bonus it outweighed the small combat differences between classes and put every unit on a mount, so roles are judged on combat alone and reach is shown beside them. 'duel' is the old single score (one-on-one duels against every enemy in the chapter roster) kept for comparison; it is slow.

rolled.note: How a role's leading paths are told apart. The 'top' paths by score are each replayed 'runs' times with level-ups actually rolled, every path with the same dice. The leader is the path with the best rolled average; another path is as good as the leader when the leader beats it in fewer than 'winShare' of those playthroughs, or by less than 'minGap' points on average. Of the paths that are as good, the one needing the least training is recommended. --runs 0 skips the replay and falls back to 'tolerance'.

tolerance.note: Only used when nothing is rolled (--runs 0): paths within this many points of a role's best path are treated as equally good; among them the one needing the least training is recommended.

notModeled: Combat arts themselves (only an ability's bonus for using one is counted, see 'abilities'), Blaze arts, gambits/battalions and bloodmarks. Personal and level-up abilities are applied only where their text is a plain combat or healing modifier; the rest are listed per unit by `char`.
Mounts' bonus stats and growths, shields, terrain, supports, weapon forging and durability.
Mastery abilities and abilities learned by skill rank (only always-on class abilities such as 'Axe Hit +5' are applied).
Certification odds and the Arena: skill ranks are estimated from time spent in each class (see 'skills'), not simulated.
Stat caps (none published) and the level-scaling growth of Charioteer / Elephant Rider. Elephant Rider is excluded because its attack has no published stats.
Canto and other mount abilities, attack range beyond choosing the best range, ally buffs and enemy debuffs.
